Beds are [[Player base|base]] structures used for sleeping and setting the player's respawn point.

== Sleeping ==
{{Main|Sleeping}}
It is possible to sleep in a bed after a player has claimed one. Sleeping skips the game clock to the next morning. The game will progress in fast-forward while the player sleeps, meaning that crafting stations that process materials will continue working. This can make sleeping advantageous if the player is attempting to refine a large volume of materials quickly.

It is only possible to sleep if:

# It is [[Day and Night Cycle|afternoon or night]].
# There are no enemies nearby.
# The bed has a roof and 80% [[cover]].
# There is a fire nearby.
# The player is not wet.

There is a 10% chance for the player  to [[Sleeping#Dreams|dream]] while sleeping on a bed.

== Claiming ==
A bed can be claimed when it has a roof and 80% [[cover]]. Press [E] while looking directly at a bed to claim it. The most recent bed claimed by a player will serve as their respawn point. This can be used strategically by building small outposts outside of dungeons or other dangerous areas and placing a bed inside, allowing the player to quickly return and reattempt the area.

Once a bed has been claimed by a player, other players cannot override their claim unless the bed is destroyed and re-placed.

If your bed (spawn point) is destroyed and you die, you will respawn at the [[Sacrificial Stones]].

== Notes ==
* A Bed will increase the [[Comfort]] level by 1.
* If a player sleeps in a bed that is very close to a roof, it is possible to wake up on the other side of the roof.

'''Campfires''' are [[Player base|base]] structures used for cooking, sleeping and warmth.

They do not require a [[Workbench]] or any other structure to build.
== Notes ==
* A Campfire can only be built on the ground, natural rocks or player placed stone structures.
* Untamed [[Boar|Boars]], [[Greyling|Greylings]], [[Greydwarf|Greydwarfs]] and [[Neck|Necks]] fear fire and will flee from it.
* [[Greydwarf Brute]]s and [[Greydwarf Shaman]]s do not fear fire and will attack the player regardless of Campfire proximity.
* A Campfire must be fueled with [[Wood]] in order to function.
* Campfires stop working if exposed to rainy weather without a roof.
* Campfires stop working if exposed to strong wind without 70% [[cover]].
* Active Campfires create [[smoke]]. If the Campfire is created within an enclosed space, the smoke can build up, causing any players inside to be [[Smoked]] and take 2 hp/tick damage. To safely place a Campfire indoors, the interior space must be large enough to let the smoke naturally dissipate or be vented out through a chimney or other holes.
** The smoke appears to have a 1 block diameter, so to use multiple Campfires, larger or more chimneys will become necessary.
* The [[Fire Effect]] for the Campfire extends for about 8 meters (Measuring from the closest the player can stand without setting themselves on fire).
* [[Wet Effect|Wet]] players dry significantly faster when close to Campfires.
* It can be used for cooking (in combination with a [[Cooking Station]] or a [[Cauldron]] or a combination of both).
* It is required for a [[Bed]] to be used for sleeping, but will not prevent it from being a spawn point.
* Destroying the Campfire with a [[Hammer]] will yield back just the 5 [[Stone]]s used for construction. All [[Wood]] that was used as fuel and for the initial construction will <u>not</u> be dropped.
* With 1/10 fuel, a Campfire will last for 1 hour and 23 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Campfire should burn for 13 hours and 53 minutes. This duration is the same for the [[Bonfire]].
* A Campfire will take 10 damage every time it sets an entity on fire.
* One of the few base structures that is not a priority target for creatures.

Hearths are [[Player base|base]] structures used for cooking, sleeping and warmth.

They require [[Stonecutter]] to be built.

== Notes ==
* The hearth has an approximate [[Fire Effect]] range of 12 meters (Measured from the closest you can stand).
* The hearth is used to make a bigger fire than the [[Campfire]]. More [[Cooking Station|cooking stations]] can be placed on the hearth.
* Press [E] to use wood as a fuel.
* Hearths stop working if exposed to rain without a roof.
* Hearths stop working if exposed to strong wind without 70% [[cover]].
* Active hearths create [[smoke]].
* The hearth must be built on something strong and sturdy such as stone floor, the ground, or pillars to support it. If placed on an unsupported wood floor, the Hearth will break upon placement; to place on a wooden floor, the floor must either be on the ground or supported by stone or [[Wood Iron Beam|Wood iron beams]].
* With 1/20 fuel, a Hearth will last for 1 hour and 23 minutes. At maximum capacity a Hearth should burn for 27 hours and 47 minutes.
* Sitting next to the hearth without [[Shelter Effect|shelter]] or being sheltered but farther than 8 meters away from the hearth will only result in the providing 1 [[comfort]]. The player must be sheltered and also in an 8 meter range from the hearth in order for the hearth to provide 2 comfort.
* Hearths will take 10 damage every time it sets an entity on fire.

Bonfires are [[Player base|base]] structures used for cooking, sleeping and warmth.

Compared to [[Campfire]]s, they provide fire over a larger area and do not go out during rain.
== Notes ==
* Bonfires can only be placed on the ground and on stone structures.
* Multiple [[Cooking Station]]s can be placed around the Bonfire, however, the [[Cauldron]] does not work as it needs the fire directly underneath it.
* A Bonfire must be fueled with [[Wood]] in order to function. Unlike the [[Campfire]], it requires fueling with Wood immediately after placement in order to burn.
* With 1/10 fuel, a Bonfire will last for roughly 1 hour and 23 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Bonfire should burn for roughly 13 hours and 53 minutes. This duration is the same for the [[Campfire]].
* Bonfires in captured [[Fuling Village]]s can be recycled for their materials, including the [[Surtling Core]], if a Workbench is built in their vicinity.
* When exposed to rain without roof or strong wind without 70% [[cover]], the fire gets dimmer and the [[Fire Effect]] radius drops from 15 meters to 12 meters.
* Active bonfires create [[smoke]].
* Using a [[Surtling Core]] or [[Black Core]] on a bonfire produces a firework-like effect, that is visible to players outside the normal render distance.
* One of the few base structures that is not a priority target for creatures.

The '''Hanging brazier''' is a light source that can be placed on the underside of a surface, and must be built within the range of a [[Forge]].

==Usage==
The Hanging brazier has all the same functions as a [[Campfire]] and is a [[Player base|base]] structure.

Hanging braziers are fueled with [[Coal]]. With 1/5 fuel, a Hanging brazier will last for 5 hours and 33 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Hanging brazier should burn for 27 hours and 47 minutes. It can be used for cooking, however, it does not fit easily like a [[Campfire]] does.

Hanging 2–6 meters off the ground (measuring from where the chain connects), the [[Fire Effect]] extends out 9 meters. The horizontal distance begins to drop off if hanging from 7 meters high or higher.

==Notes==
* If part of its supporting structure is destroyed, it will not collapse as long as there is another structure that is connected to the ground within ~1 meter of the brazier.
* Destroying the Hanging brazier with a [[Hammer]] will not yield back any [[Coal]] and will only return the 5 [[Bronze]] and 1 [[Chain]] used for its construction. All Coal used as fuel and for the initial construction will <u>not</u> be dropped.
* Hanging braziers stop working if exposed to rainy weather without a roof.

The '''Maypole''' is a [[Seasonal events|seasonal]] structure that can be built exclusively during the midsummer season. It also can be found rarely in the middle of [[Abandoned Village]]s within the [[Meadows]]. Its sole purpose is to increase [[Comfort]] by 1.

== Availability ==
Maypoles generate during world generation. One or more can be found in a world. They will not respawn once destroyed.

From {{#formatdate:1 Jun|dmy}} – {{#formatdate:6 Jul|dmy}}, Maypoles are made temporarily buildable to celebrate Midsummer and then unbuildable the rest of the year. Player-placed Maypoles function identically to the natural ones and remain in the world after the Midsummer season has ended.

The '''Hot tub''' is a decorative item that can be placed on any flooring, and can be built using the [[Hammer]] within the range of a [[Workbench]]. It requires [[Wood]] as fuel and produces smoke while lit. The Hot Tub also increases the [[Comfort]] level by 2 when fueled.

Uniquely, the hot tub will allow a player to gain the [[Rested Effect]] while wet, something that is not normally possible.

Destroying the hot tub with a hammer will not yield back any wood used for fuel and will only return the materials used for its construction. All wood used as fuel will '''not''' be dropped.

While working, it provides the [[Fire Effect]] but only for about one meter around it.

== Notes ==
* A fueled hot tub will eventually kill the player in the Ashlands after spending too much time inside. This occurs in the same way as all water found in the Ashlands biome. In other biomes, the player character can remain in a hot tub indefinitely without being damaged by the water.

The '''Iron Fire Pit''' is a light source that can be placed on any surface. 

==Usage==
The Iron Fire Pit has all the same functions as a [[Campfire]] and is a [[Player base|base]] structure.

Iron Fire Pits are fueled with [[Wood]]. With 1/10 fuel, an Iron Fire Pit will last for roughly 1 hour and 23 minutes. At maximum capacity, an Iron Fire Pit should burn for roughly 13 hours and 53 minutes. It can be used for cooking, however, it does not fit easily like a [[Campfire]] does.

The [[Fire Effect]] for the Iron Fire Pit extends for about 7–8 meters.

== Notes ==
* Destroying the Iron Fire Pit with a [[Hammer]] will not yield back any [[Wood]] and will only return the [[Iron Pit]] used for its construction. All Wood used as fuel and for the initial construction will <u>not</u> be dropped.
* Iron Fire Pits can be found in [[Dvergr Charred Tower Ruins]] in the [[Ashlands]], 1 Iron pit will drop if destroyed, however, they are protected by the Dvergr's [[Ward]].
* Iron Fire Pits stop working if exposed to rainy weather without a roof.

== Trivia ==
* Iron Fire Pit is an item which got introduced in the [[Version history#0.217.14_-_Hildir's_Request|Hildir's Request update]].

The '''Blue standing brazier''' is a light source that can be placed on any surface, and must be built within the range of a [[Forge]]. 

==Usage==
The Blue standing brazier has all the same functions as a [[Campfire]] and is a [[Player base|base]] structure.

Blue standing braziers are fueled with [[Greydwarf Eye]]s. With 1/5 fuel, a Blue standing brazier will last for 5 hours and 33 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Blue standing brazier should burn for 27 hours and 47 minutes. It can be used for cooking, however, it does not fit easily like a [[Campfire]] does.

The [[Fire Effect]] for the Blue standing brazier extends for about 4–5 meters (Measured from the closest the player can stand without setting themselves on fire).

==Notes==
* Destroying the Blue standing brazier with a [[Hammer]] will not yield back any [[Greydwarf Eye]]s and will only return the 5 [[Bronze]] and 3 [[Fenris Claw]]s used for its construction. All Greydwarf eyes used as fuel and for the initial construction will <u>not</u> be dropped.
* Blue standing braziers found in [[Howling Cavern]] can be destroyed for up to 2 Coal and sometimes 1 Bronze.
* Blue standing braziers stop working if exposed to rainy weather without a roof.

'''Ashwood beds''' are [[Player base|base]] structures used for sleeping and setting the player's respawn point. Despite being obtainable later than [[Dragon Bed]]s, they only give 1 [[Comfort]], as much as a regular [[bed]].

== Sleeping ==
{{#lsth:Bed|Sleeping}}
== Notes ==
A bed can be claimed when it has a roof and 80% [[cover]]. Press [E] while looking directly at a bed to claim it.

The most recent bed claimed by a player will serve as their respawn point. This can be used strategically by building small outposts outside of dungeons or other dangerous areas and placing a bed inside, allowing the player to quickly return and reattempt the area.

Once a bed has been claimed by a player, other players cannot override their claim unless the bed is destroyed and re-placed.

If your bed (spawn point) is destroyed and you die, you will respawn at the starting location.

An ashwood bed will increase the [[Comfort]] level by 1.

If a player sleeps in a bed that is very close to a roof, it is possible to wake up on the other side of the roof.
